content: Stand firm, for the tempest will not last forever, but the dignity of your soul will endure.
author: Seneca
sourceWork: De Tranquillitate Animi (On Tranquility of Mind)
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Hardship is not an unfair interruption to your real life—it is the very forge in which character is tempered. No one develops deep wisdom, empathy, or stamina by cruising down an easy path without resistance.

Across his life and work, Seneca saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Like a tree that develops deeper roots when buffeted by winter gales, your past trials gave you a reservoir of strength you didn't know you possessed. You are more durable than your anxious thoughts give you credit for.
reflectionPrompt: What current difficulty or obstacle are you facing that could become your greatest training ground?
